_comment: The TradingRuntime class only shrinks. Raise this only with the owner's
sign-off and a recorded reason, the same rule structure_baseline.json
carries -- these two numbers describe the same class and move together.
Raised once, 2026-08-27, from 79 to 88. The upstream merge (1e383fe)
added nine methods: six supervisor loops (_auto_template_loop,
_closed_market_queue_loop, _ea_link_watchdog_loop, _ref_backfill_loop,
_signal_snapshot_loop, _revalidate_pending_orders) plus close_cmd,
schedule_profit_sync and _await_trade_promotion.
None of them is a leaked implementation of the kind M4 B3-B9 deleted --
the public surface still matches facade_allowlist.json exactly, and six
of the nine are loops a supervisor is supposed to own. Getting back to
79 means removing whole responsibilities, and the biggest ones left
(_close_full_after_tps, _cmd_close) are close-path and frozen.
Two of the nine loop BODIES were relocated into their services before
this rise, with 20 new tests. That is the shape any future reduction
should take: the method stays, the decision logic leaves.
Raised again, 2026-09-03, from 88 to 89, owner sign-off in-session.
get_ticks_range() forwards to the bridge, same one-line shape as every
other market-data method here (get_candles_for_symbol, get_tick, ...).
docs/todo/backtest/010 phase 1: the backtest's tick-walking simulator
needs tick history, and the live bridge connection only exists inside
this class -- there is no side door that reaches it without going
through the facade.
Raised again, 2026-09-19, from 89 to 90, owner sign-off in-session.
get_deal_history() forwards to the bridge, the same one-line shape as
get_ticks_range above. The Analysis tab's deal-level trade table is the
last thing the React port could not build: the NiceGUI page read
engine._bridge.get_deal_history() directly, which the controller boundary
forbids, and there is no side door to the live bridge that does not go
through this class. The alternative considered was a service function
taking the engine, which fails test_no_production_code_reaches_into_a_
runtime_private because that test derives its leak set from the runtime's
own members.
Deliberately ONE method, not two. The table's spread column also wanted
get_tick_at() to backfill uncached tickets; it renders from the existing
spread cache instead and shows an em dash where there is none. A second
name is a second decision.
Raised again, 2026-09-21, from 90 to 91, owner sign-off in-session.
get_open_positions_view() answers two reports from the same day: the
Positions table showed an em dash for P&L on every open position, and it
showed one position where MT5 had two.
Both need the LIVE bridge. mt5_profit is only written when a trade
closes, so a running P&L can only come from the broker's /positions
payload; and a position opened by hand in MetaTrader has no row in
vantage_simulated_trades at all, so it can only come from the same place.
Same reasoning as get_deal_history above, and the same alternatives were
rejected for the same reasons: there is no side door to the bridge that
does not go through this class, and a service function taking the engine
fails test_no_production_code_reaches_into_a_runtime_private.
The method is READ-ONLY and holds no logic: it hands the already-read
trade rows and the bridge to services/positions/live_view.py. Nothing
here places, closes or sizes anything, and the running figure is never
written back to mt5_profit -- that column stays the realised one that
record_close, the balance report and the history importer read.
get_untracked_mt5_positions was NOT reused for it. It filters the live
payload down to the untracked rows, which is the half this needs least;
the running P&L belongs to the tracked ones it discards.
